byte_identical_audit_note: n_byte_identical_input_dupes counts rows whose exact noisy_text string recurs under >1 corpus ANYWHERE in the table (global check, not paired by message/cer_target/replicate/model key). A stricter paired check (same key, AUTH vs CTRL) finds only 19838 of 91700 CTRL rows are byte-identical to their AUTH twin -- almost entirely a cer_target=0.0 artifact (0 realized errors always yields noisy_text == intended_text). Most CTRL rows use an INDEPENDENT corruption draw from AUTH for the same underlying message: CTRL and AUTH are twins in MESSAGE IDENTITY, not in literal corrupted-input bytes.
